description:
Splitting and reassembly (protocol.md section 6.1). Each split case names a payload built as {key: unit repeated times} -- generative rather than literal, following size_cases in framing.json, so a 96 KB vector costs no 96 KB of corpus. A conforming implementation must serialize that payload, split it, and produce exactly the segment byte lengths given, then rebuild the payload by concatenating the segments as UTF-8 bytes.

What this family uniquely proves: that all seven implementations put the cuts in the SAME places. Nothing else can see that. The bounds (chunk count, buffer, in-flight count, timeout) are pinned by the per-language unit suites and the negative cases in messages.json; the wire shape is pinned by messages.json. This file deliberately does not duplicate either.

Vectors avoid the characters < > and & on purpose. Go's encoding/json escapes them to \u003c, \u003e and \u0026 by default where the other six emit them raw, which would move Go's cuts; go/message/chunk.go disables that for splitting so the fleet agrees, and these vectors would catch it coming back.

split_cases.name: whole-well-under-the-segment-maximum
split_cases.note: A payload that fits travels whole: one message, payload present, no seg.

split_cases.name: whole-exactly-at-the-segment-maximum
split_cases.note: The boundary itself is still whole -- the cap is inclusive, so a payload serializing to exactly 24000 bytes is not split.

split_cases.name: two-segments-one-byte-over
split_cases.note: One byte past the maximum is the smallest split there is, and its second segment is a single byte.

split_cases.name: five-segments-ascii
split_cases.note: 96000 filler bytes: four full segments and a short tail.

split_cases.name: multi-byte-cut-needs-back-off
split_cases.note: Every character is 3 UTF-8 bytes and the 7-byte key prefix leaves 24000 misaligned with the character grid, so a naive byte cut would split a character. The segment lengths below are therefore NOT all 24000: the first cut walks back to the boundary. A port slicing code points rather than bytes, or forgetting the back-off, disagrees here and nowhere else.

split_cases.name: multi-byte-cut-already-aligned
split_cases.note: The same payload with a 9-byte key prefix, which leaves 24000 aligned with the 3-byte character grid. Pinned alongside the case above so the back-off is shown to fire only when it must, rather than shortening every cut.
